source_text:
Τοιούτοις οὖν ὑποδείγμασιν κολληθῆναι καὶ ἡμᾶς δεῖ, ἀδελφοί.
γέγραπται γάρ: Κολλᾶσθε τοῖς ἁγίοις, ὅτι οἱ κολλώμενοι αὐτοῖς ἁγιασθήσονται.
καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἑτέρῳ τόπῳ λέγει: Μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἀθῷον ἀθῷος ἔσῃ καὶ μετὰ ἐκλεκτοῦ ἐκλεκτὸς ἔσῃ. καὶ μετὰ στρεβλοῦ διαστρέψεις.
κολληθῶμεν οὖν τοῖς ἀθῴοις καὶ δικαίοις: εἰσὶν δὲ οὗτοι ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ.
ἱνατί ἔρεις καὶ θυμοὶ καὶ διχοστασίαι καὶ σχίσματα πόλεμός τε ἐν ὑμῖν;
ἢ οὐχὶ ἕνα θεὸν ἔχομεν καὶ ἔνα Χριστὸν καὶ ἓν πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος τὸ ἐκχυθὲν ἐφ̓ ἡμᾶς; καὶ μία κλῆσις ἐν Χριστῷ;
ἱνατί διέλκομεν καὶ διασπῶμεν τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ στασιάζομεν πρὸς τὸ σῶμα τὸ ἴδιον, καὶ εἰς τοσαύτην ἀπόνοιαν ἐρχόμεθα, ὥστε ἐπιλαθέσθαι ἡμᾶς, ὅτι μέλη ἐσμὲν ἀλλήλων; μνήσθητε τῶν λόγων τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
εἶπεν γάρ: Οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ: καλὸν ἦν αὐτῷ, εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη, ἦ ἕνα τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν μου σκανδαλίσαι κρεῖττον ἢν αὐτῷ περιτεθῆναι μύλον καὶ καταπον τισθῆναι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἢ ἕνα τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν μου διαστρέψαι.
τὸ σχίσμα ὑμῶν πολλοὺς διέστρεψεν, πολλοὺς εἰς ἀθυμίαν ἔβαλεν, πολλοὺς: εἰς δισταγμόν, τοὺς πάντας ἡμᾶς εἰς λύπην: καὶ ἐπίμονος ἀμῶν ἐστιν ἡ στάσις.
thought_title: Cling to the holy and stop tearing Christ's body
orientation: The Roman church has just finished praising those who endured under envy, and now turns directly to the Corinthians with a command to join themselves to the holy and a rebuke for their divisions.
pass_a_gloss: To such examples to be joined also us it is necessary, brothers. For it is written: Be joined to the holy ones, because the ones being joined to them will be made holy. And again in another place he says: With an innocent man innocent you will be, and with an elect one elect you will be. And with a crooked one you will be perverted. Let us be joined therefore to the innocent and righteous ones; and these are the elect of God. Why are there strifes and angers and dissensions and divisions and war among you? Or do we not have one God and one Christ and one spirit of grace, the one poured out upon us? And one calling in Christ? Why do we tear apart and rip apart the members of Christ and make faction against our own body, and come to such madness, so as to forget us, that members we are of one another? Remember the words of the Lord Jesus. For he said: Woe to that man; good it was for him, if he had not been born, than one of my elect to scandalize; better it was for him to have a millstone put around and to be sunk into the sea, than one of my elect to pervert. Your division has perverted many, has thrown many into despondency, many into doubt, all of us into grief; and persistent is your faction.

choices.why: The verb means to cling or adhere closely; 'joined' keeps the physical intimacy of the metaphor without the informal tone of 'cling' in a formal letter.
The adjective describes moral perversity as twistedness; 'crooked' preserves the spatial metaphor of the source.
The noun means standing apart, factional division; 'dissensions' captures the active disagreement while distinguishing it from σχίσματα.
The glossary requires 'division' for σχίσμα; the plural here refers to the multiple splits in the Corinthian community.
The noun denotes loss of right thinking, irrational folly; 'madness' conveys the severity of the rebuke.
The glossary requires 'faction' for στάσις; the verb form here means to engage in factional strife against one's own body.

bible_refs.note: Μετὰ ἀνδρὸς ἀθῷον ἀθῷος ἔσῃ καὶ μετὰ ἐκλεκτοῦ ἐκλεκτὸς ἔσῃ. καὶ μετὰ στρεβλοῦ διαστρέψεις.
Οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ: καλὸν ἦν αὐτῷ, εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη
κρεῖττον ἢν αὐτῷ περιτεθῆναι μύλον καὶ καταποντισθῆναι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἢ ἕνα τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν μου διαστρέψαι

pass_b_english: So we too must hold fast to such examples, brothers and sisters.
For it is written: “Join yourselves to the holy ones, because those who join themselves to them will be made holy.”
And again in another place he says: “With an innocent man you will be innocent, and with one of the elect you will be elect, and with a crooked one you will be perverted.”
Let us be joined, then, to the innocent and the righteous, and these are the elect of God.
Why are there strifes and outbursts of anger and dissensions and divisions and war among you?
Do we not have one God and one Christ and one Spirit of grace poured out upon us, and one calling in Christ?
Why do we tear apart and rip apart the members of Christ, and make faction against our own body, and reach such madness that we forget that we are members of one another?
Remember the words of the Lord Jesus.

For he said: “Woe to that man! It would have been good for him if he had not been born, than to cause one of my elect to stumble. It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and be drowned in the sea, than to pervert one of my elect.”
Your division has perverted many, thrown many into despair, many into doubt, all of us into grief, and your faction persists.
notes: The source text contains 'καταπον τισθῆναι' with a space in the middle; this is likely a typographical or OCR artifact for καταποντισθῆναι (to be sunk). The gloss treats it as the full verb.
The phrase 'ἐπίμονος ἀμῶν ἐστιν ἡ στάσις' appears to have 'ἀμῶν' where 'ἡμῶν' (our) is expected; the gloss renders it as 'your faction is persistent' based on context, but the reading is uncertain.

problems.quote: rather than to cause one of my elect to stumble
problems.source_quote: ἢ ἕνα τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν μου σκανδαλίσαι
problems.why: English adds 'rather than to cause...to stumble' as if part of first clause, but Greek has two separate 'better' comparisons.
problems.fix: than to cause one of my elect to stumble. Better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and be drowned in the sea, than to pervert one of my elect.
problems.ruling: Greek compares causing a stumble vs millstone; English flips comparison, misrepresenting ‘better than’ as ‘rather than’.

problems.quote: Why do we tear apart and rip open the members of Christ, and make faction against our own body, and reach such madness that we forget that we are members of one another?
problems.source_quote: ἱνατί διέλκομεν καὶ διασπῶμεν τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ στασιάζομεν πρὸς τὸ σῶμα τὸ ἴδιον, …
problems.why: The verb διέλκομεν “cross over” is omitted from the English list of actions.
problems.fix: Why do we cross over, tear apart and rip open the members of Christ, make faction against our own body, and reach such madness…
problems.ruling: διέλκομεν ('tear apart, lacerate') omitted; only διασπῶμεν rendered, losing violent imagery.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'the elect of God' is not a real problem in this passage: the English already uses 'the elect of God' consistently with the source's 'ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ'.
The glossary issue about 'the Master' is not present in this passage: the English uses 'Lord' for 'κυρίου', which is consistent with the brief's divine title guidance.
The scripture citation issue is not a translation problem: the source itself conflates Gospel sayings without citation, and the English faithfully renders the source's wording.

polish.changed: Clarified the quotation of Jesus by smoothing the comparison, removed the redundant 'cross over' from the list of violent actions, and adjusted punctuation to make the flow of thought easier to follow aloud.

Clarified the flow of argument by keeping the speaker of each scriptural quotation explicit, preserving every claim and quotation exactly, and smoothing sentence rhythm for public reading without adding or removing content.

refereed.source_quote: καὶ ἐπίμονος ἀμῶν ἐστιν ἡ στάσις.
refereed.why: ἀμῶν is Koine ἡμῶν (“our”). The English makes the persisting faction the Corinthians’ alone.
refereed.ruling: ἀμῶν = ἡμῶν 'our'; preceded by 'all of us'. English 'your faction persists' changes ownership/agency; should be 'our' (the strife/faction among us persists).
